entries.definition: Entity on whose behalf an action or claim is represented.
Entity that performed or is reported to have performed an action.
Assertion binding an identifier or credential to an actor.
Identified source from which an authority claim originates.
Bounded actions, targets, resources, and constraints to which authority evidence refers.
Recorded transfer of bounded authority from a source to a delegate.
Producer-supplied authority assertion without independent authority verification.
Declared objective associated with a subject or proposed action.
Bounded act proposed, attempted, observed, or completed.
Invocation or attempted invocation of a named tool.
Limit within which an authority claim may be evaluated.
Limit between evidence interpretation and an external execution decision.
Limit of effects attributable to a bounded action or transition.
Context and time in which an institution relies on evidence.
Observed or asserted change associated with an action.
Result state observed or asserted after an action or transition.
Bound movement from one identified state to another.
Addressable artifact or record offered as evidence.
Recorded observation made by an identified source or method.
Signed or attributable assertion by an identified attester.
Bounded act that checks a stated property using an identified method and verifier.
Evaluated proposition with an explicit subject and boundaries.
Subject, scope, time, and provenance boundary of a claim.
Relation between bound evidence and a bound claim.
Entity or process that emitted or packaged evidence.
Entity or process that performed a bounded verification.
Ordered source and transformation history of an artifact or semantic result.
Evaluation of whether evidence remains a valid basis at reliance time.
Human or institutional review event over a bound subject.
External or Guard report expression about a reviewed evidence state, retaining residual uncertainty.

boundaries.example: A signed log exists, so the actor is assumed authorized.
boundaries.counterexample: A separate current delegation explicitly binds actor, action, target, and time.

boundaries.example: A risk assessment passes, so execution is treated as authorized.
boundaries.counterexample: Assessment and applicable external authority are evaluated as distinct claims.

boundaries.example: A token can write a repository, so every write is authorized.
boundaries.counterexample: IAM evidence separately binds the exact path, action, and time.

boundaries.example: A runtime has a deploy tool, so deployment is authorized.
boundaries.counterexample: A current scoped authority record separately covers deployment.

boundaries.example: Authentication proves the caller may approve a release.
boundaries.counterexample: Verified identity plus current code-owner delegation permits separate authority evaluation.

boundaries.example: Tests pass, so Guard authorizes merge or deploy.
boundaries.counterexample: An external system may decide using tests and separately established authority.

boundaries.example: A producer log says a test passed, so it is independently verified.
boundaries.counterexample: A separate verifier replays the bound artifact and records method and limitations.

boundaries.example: A tool trace exists, so the workflow is fully evidenced.
boundaries.counterexample: The trace is complete for a bounded claim and combined with required artifacts.

boundaries.example: SHA-256 matches, so the artifact contents are true.
boundaries.counterexample: Hash preservation and separate content verification support distinct claims.

boundaries.example: A valid signature makes every signed assertion correct.
boundaries.counterexample: Signature authenticates the issuer while an independent check evaluates correctness.

boundaries.example: A test report exists, so release evidence is sufficient.
boundaries.counterexample: The report covers the bound candidate and all claim-specific requirements.

boundaries.example: Every manifest item exists, so the change is correct.
boundaries.counterexample: Complete inventory plus bound verification supports only the checked property.

boundaries.example: Deployment returned success, so production behavior is correct.
boundaries.counterexample: Bound health observations verify specified postconditions.

boundaries.example: Error rate fell after deployment, so deployment caused it.
boundaries.counterexample: A bounded experiment may separately support attribution.

boundaries.example: A credential was valid last week, so it is valid now.
boundaries.counterexample: Revocation and expiry sources resolve to current at reliance time.

boundaries.example: The same tools remain available, so authority remains valid.
boundaries.counterexample: Current authority is independently re-evaluated.

boundaries.example: Read authority is delegated and treated as read/write authority.
boundaries.counterexample: Delegate scope is no broader than a verified delegable source.

boundaries.example: An old approval note is applied to a different commit.
boundaries.counterexample: Approval binds the same commit, scope, authorized reviewer, and current time.

boundaries.example: A rule identifier matches, so the action is legally compliant.
boundaries.counterexample: An accountable external owner makes a separate determination.

boundaries.example: Framework controls are mapped, so the system is certified.
boundaries.counterexample: An authorized external body may issue a separate certification.

boundaries.example: Human and Guard results differ, so one is wrong.
boundaries.counterexample: A bound rule and facts may establish contradiction.

boundaries.example: CI metadata contains verified=true, so it is independently verified.
boundaries.counterexample: A separate verifier checks the underlying artifact.

boundaries.example: A rollback script exists, so rollback is effective.
boundaries.counterexample: A recovery exercise verifies it against the candidate environment.

boundaries.example: A reviewer name exists, so oversight was meaningful.
boundaries.counterexample: An authorized reviewer inspected the bound subject and could intervene.
